summary: It's a tight two-player bluffing and hand-management duel where you fight over three theaters and must decide when to play a strong card for tempo versus holding it as a Reserve to threaten a swing. Games are fast and tense, often decided by a single well-timed Support, Retreat, or Redeploy special ability that flips a losing theater.
praised: Huge depth from a tiny card pool
Elegant special-ability text that creates constant bluffing and mind games
New theaters (Intelligence, Diplomacy, Economics) add fresh tactical texture without bloating the game
Easy to teach, hard to master
criticised: Strictly two-player, so it can't flex to groups
Some new cards/theaters seen as less balanced or elegant than the original six
Thin, abstract theme (WWII/animal art skin) that doesn't add narrative weight
Requires the base game or its own theaters to reach 'Epic Mode' variety

interaction.kind: direct card-play conflict and bluffing over shared theaters

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The player controlling more theaters (by total card value) at the end of the round wins, so it comes down to concentrating strength and timing key plays across just three or five theaters

_name: Air, Land, & Sea: Spies, Lies, & Supplies
